stem: A supervisor can either buy more warning signs or eliminate a recurring trip hazard caused by a poorly routed hose. Which action follows stronger hazard-control logic?
choices: Reroute or engineer out the hose hazard, then use signs only if residual risk remains
Buy more signs because warnings always outrank physical controls
Do nothing because workers already know the hose is there
Require workers to step over it more carefully
rationale: Removing or engineering out a hazard is generally stronger than relying only on warnings or worker behavior.
